quickStart.title: Read messages from a WebSocket feed
quickStart.description: Replace the example URL with a feed you can access. Subscribe, wait briefly for messages, read the buffer, then unsubscribe.
quickStart.note: The query can return no rows if no messages arrive. Buffers live in the DuckDB process; they are not a durable message store.
quickStart.requirements: Supply a working WebSocket URL. `stream.example.com` is a placeholder, not a demo service.

introduction.title: Collect live messages for SQL queries
paragraphs: Radio connects to WebSocket feeds or Redis Pub/Sub channels and buffers incoming messages inside the DuckDB process. SQL functions read those messages as rows and can queue outgoing messages.

Use it to inspect a live feed or combine recent events with local data. You need an accessible messaging endpoint. The buffers are temporary, so save messages to a table when you need to retain them beyond the running session.
